correctness.rationale: For the stated reciprocal two-agent, unit-self-weight and no-rate-multiplier model, the gap obeys d'=-2wφ(d)d/(1+w); the mean is conserved. Dividing the logistic equation by 1−w² gives exactly F'(d)d', so C=artanh(w)−F(d) is constant. Positivity and strict finite-time bounds follow from the multiplicative ODE factors; d=2 is inward-pointing, not an invariant face as the blanket wording in the proof suggests. The decreasing gap has a limit, and the weight has a limit because its derivative changes sign at most once. A positive limiting gap forces w→0; d→0 forces w→1 by logistic comparison. F decreases to its unique minimum 0 at r, increases thereafter, and diverges at zero. For d0>r, C<0 forces stagnation at the unique right-branch root F(d∞)=−C, C=0 forces approach to r from above, and C>0 forces a crossing below r and hence consensus. For d0≤r the tie increases once d<r, so consensus follows. Writing a=−φ'(r)>0 gives F(r+z)=(a/r)z²+O(z³) and z'=−az²+O(z³), so (1/z)'→a; the two critical limits and both logarithmic off-critical rates follow by time averaging. The exponential example also differentiates correctly. The rational-kernel checker comment at line 66 misstates F''(1), which is 1/2, not 1/4; the latter is the quadratic Taylor coefficient and the checked formula and theorem use the correct value.
residual_risks: Finite quadrature corroborates a rational-kernel example only. The proof needs the stated normalization, interior initial tie and transverse crossing for the quoted powers. No larger-network classification or formal certification is inferred.
